claims.text: In 1967 another 300,000 Palestinians fled from the West Bank and Gaza, about 200,000 to Jordan; approximately 180,000 were first-time refugees and the rest 1948 refugees uprooted a second time.

In June 1967 the people of Imwas, Yalo and Beit Nuba, some 8,000, were ordered to march toward Ramallah and their villages razed on the orders of Yitzhak Rabin; Dayan wrote the houses were destroyed 'not in battle, but as punishment'; in 1973 JNF Canada raised $5 million for Canada Park on the site; Israel said the residents had joined attacks on Jerusalem in 1948 and an Egyptian commando raid.

On 27–28 June 1967 Israel applied its law to about 70 km² added to Jerusalem: about 6 km² of Jordanian East Jerusalem and 64 km² from 28 villages and parts of Bethlehem and Beit Jala; the Mughrabi Quarter was bulldozed to expand the Western Wall plaza; UNSC Resolution 252 (21 May 1968) declared the measures invalid; Resolution 478 (1980) declared the Jerusalem Law null and void.

Resolution 242 (22 Nov 1967, unanimous) emphasized 'the inadmissibility of the acquisition of territory by war', called for 'Withdrawal of Israeli armed forces from territories occupied in the recent conflict', the right of every state to live 'within secure and recognized boundaries', and a 'just settlement of the refugee problem'; the English omits 'the' while the French reads 'des territoires occupés'; its drafters said the omission was deliberate and that it 'neither commands nor prohibits total withdrawal'.

In September 1967 the Foreign Ministry's legal counsel Theodor Meron, asked by the Prime Minister's Office, concluded that 'civilian settlement in the administered territories contravenes the explicit provisions of the Fourth Geneva Convention'; the cabinet then approved Eshkol's announcement of an 'outpost' at Kfar Etzion presented as a Nahal army base though it had no connection to the military.

On 27 July 1967 Yigal Allon presented a plan to keep most of the Jordan Valley, East Jerusalem and the Etzion area and offer the populated hill areas to Jordan; never formally endorsed by the cabinet; Hussein rejected it; settlement policy in the first decade largely followed it.

In 1929, 67 Jews were killed by Arab rioters in Hebron; in 1968 a group led by Rabbi Moshe Levinger rented Hebron's main hotel and refused to leave, with tacit support from Eshkol and Allon; they were moved to an army camp and Kiryat Arba was established; from 1979 settlers took over Beit Hadassah in central Hebron.
In 2025 the West Bank settler population excluding East Jerusalem was 529,704 and about 246,000 in East Jerusalem.

Israel argues the territories did not belong to any sovereign state when captured in 1967, Jordan's claim being unrecognized; that claims based on the 1947 resolution were invalid because it was rejected; that the Fourth Convention is 'inapplicable on its face' since Common Article 2 covers 'occupation of the territory of a High Contracting Party'; it pledges compliance with 'the humanitarian and customary provisions'; critics cite Articles 1 and 4.
